# Company 045 — Autonomous Customer Support Company

**Company ID:** `company:future:045`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:045`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-045-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer messaging, refunds, account changes or public support operation.

## Business identity

Purpose: operate customer support across authorized channels using policy-grounded AI and deterministic workflows, escalating exceptions while continuously measuring correctness and customer outcomes.

Problem: support is repetitive, multilingual, knowledge-intensive and costly, yet wrong AI answers can create privacy, billing, security or reputational harm.

Value: high-coverage Tier 0/1 automation with strict identity, knowledge, action and QA boundaries.

## Product tree

Omnichannel Intake; AI Chat Support; Email Support; Voice Support; SMS/Authorized Social Support; Tier 0 Self-Service; Tier 1 Resolution; Technical Troubleshooting; Billing Support; Returns/Order Support; Account/Access Support; Knowledge Search; Case/Ticket Management; Escalation/Handoff; Customer Identity Verification; Approved Action Tools; Refund/Credit Request Preparation; Multilingual Support; Sentiment/Urgency; QA/Coaching; Workforce/Queue Analytics; Incident/Broadcast Support; Customer Portal/Bot; API/OEM; Vertical Packs; Managed Support Operations.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: channel identity, customer/account scope, consent, conversation state, ticket priority, intent, knowledge citations, policy version, allowed actions, auth level, sensitive-data redaction, SLA, sentiment, escalation reason, response approval mode, translation, attachments, fraud/security flags, QA score, resolution verification, audit.

Customers: SaaS, ecommerce, marketplaces, subscription businesses, apps, services, travel/hospitality, utilities/admin, enterprise internal support desks, platforms embedding support.

Verticals: ecommerce/returns, SaaS/technical, subscriptions/billing, travel/bookings, financial-service customer support only with strict regulated packs, healthcare administrative support, telecom, education, home services. High-risk sectors restrict autonomous actions.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Support Brain knows authorized customer/product/account context, knowledge sources, policies and prior case history. It classifies intent, reasons through troubleshooting, recommends/executes only allowed low-risk actions, detects uncertainty/security risk and escalates. It must not invent policy, expose another customer, issue unauthorized financial adjustments or bypass identity verification.

Architecture: omnichannel adapters, customer identity/session, ticket/case state machine, permission/action tools, knowledge RAG with source/version, rules/policy, fraud/security hooks, translation/speech, LLM/model routing, QA/evaluation, workflow engine, audit.

## Agent tree

Intake/Triage Agent, Knowledge Answer Agent, Technical Troubleshooting Agent, Billing Agent, Order/Returns Agent, Account Access Agent, Identity Verification Coordinator, Sentiment/Urgency Agent, Escalation Agent, Multilingual Agent, Voice Agent, QA/Policy Agent, Security/Abuse Agent, Incident Support Agent, Knowledge Gap Agent, Customer Recovery Agent, Workforce Analytics Agent.

## Deterministic services

Channel gateway; ticket/case store; customer/account resolver; auth/verification; knowledge retrieval; action/tool gateway; refund/credit policy rules; queue/SLA routing; translation/speech provider abstraction; attachment scanning; redaction; rate/abuse limits; QA sampling; audit; protected send/financial/account-action gate.

## Workflow

Inbound message/call → treat content as untrusted → identify channel/account → authenticate as needed → classify intent/risk → retrieve cited knowledge/policy → answer or propose allowed action → verify tool result → customer confirmation where appropriate → close with resolution evidence or escalate with full context → QA sample → feed knowledge gaps.

## Integrations / API / data

Helpdesk/CRM, ecommerce/order, billing/payment, identity/auth, product telemetry, status/incident, knowledge/CMS, email/SMS/voice/social, shipping/returns, scheduling, ticketing. APIs for conversations/cases/knowledge/action eligibility/escalation/QA.

Data moat: verified resolution corpus, policy/knowledge mappings, intent/error taxonomy, action outcome evidence, multilingual support patterns—customer conversations remain isolated and privacy-controlled.

## Monetization / distribution

Conversations/tickets/minutes, resolved cases, seats, channels, enterprise/private, voice usage, vertical packs, managed support, API/OEM. Distribution through helpdesk/CRM/ecommerce/SaaS marketplaces and support/BPO partners.

## Security/privacy/compliance

Inbound messages are untrusted; prompt-injection defense; identity verification; least-privilege tools; PII/PCI/health-related data boundaries; no secret exposure to model; protected refunds/account changes/sends; consent/call-recording rules; abuse/harassment safety; retention/delete/export.

## Failure / edge cases

Customer impersonation, ambiguous account, outage causing mass contacts, incorrect KB, policy conflict, emotional/escalated customer, unsupported language, malicious attachment, prompt injection, duplicate refund, tool partial failure, identity provider outage, voice transcription error. Use safe fallback, verification, rate limits and human handoff.

## Scale/platform/overlap

Small support bot → enterprise omnichannel support operations → autonomous support company/platform. Overlap #28 KB maintainer, #46 onboarding, #50 front desk, #89 support-QA. #045 owns active customer support operations.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** untrusted communications, account/identity scope, knowledge provenance, tool/action authorization, channel/brand isolation, QA/evaluation.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center communication/tool security and Brand Account identity seams likely affected after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** customer identity/tenant boundaries, comms/voice adapters, support action policy and QA.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** external support product/channels/knowledge/customer workflows.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global multilingual voice/contact-center infrastructure.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: omnichannel/chat/email/voice/SMS/social/T0/T1/technical/billing/returns/account/knowledge/cases/escalation/identity/actions/multilingual/QA/analytics/incidents/API/packs/managed.
2. Feature Tree: channel/account/consent/state/priority/intent/citations/policy/auth/redaction/SLA/sentiment/escalation/translation/attachments/security/QA/evidence.
3. Customer Tree: SaaS/commerce/marketplace/subscription/apps/services/travel/enterprise/platforms.
4. Vertical Tree: commerce/SaaS/subscription/travel/regulated support/health admin/telecom/education/home services.
5. Brain Tree: intent/troubleshooting/cited knowledge/action reasoning with identity/policy boundaries.
6. Agent Tree: triage/knowledge/technical/billing/order/account/identity/sentiment/escalation/multilingual/voice/QA/security/incident/gap/recovery/workforce.
7. Service Tree: channels/cases/customer/auth/knowledge/actions/policy/queues/speech/scan/redaction/rate/QA/audit/gates.
8. Workflow Tree: inbound→untrusted scan→identity→intent→knowledge/action→verify→resolve/escalate→QA.
9. Integration Tree: helpdesk/CRM/commerce/billing/auth/product/status/knowledge/comms/shipping/scheduling.
10. Data Tree: customers/cases/messages/intents/knowledge/policies/actions/outcomes/QA/escalations.
11. API Tree: conversations/cases/knowledge/action eligibility/escalation/QA.
12. Monetization Tree: conversations/tickets/minutes/resolutions/seats/channels/enterprise/private/packs/managed/API.
13. Distribution Tree: helpdesk/CRM/commerce/SaaS marketplaces/BPO/support ecosystems.
14. Automation Tree: triage/answers/troubleshooting/routing/QA; money/account/public actions gated.
15. Moat Tree: resolution corpus, knowledge-policy mapping, action outcomes, multilingual patterns.
16. Platform Tree: support assistant→omnichannel autonomous support→support operating platform.
17. Risk Tree: privacy, identity failure, hallucination, unauthorized refund/account action, malicious input, reputational harm.
18. Scale Tree: bot→team→enterprise/global contact-center platform.
19. Spinoff Tree: #28/#46/#50/#89 cover knowledge/onboarding/front desk/QA.
20. Command Center Dependencies: communications/brand identity, Brain/RAG, untrusted-input security, policy, customer isolation, voice, evaluation.
21. Design-Now Requirements: channel/account identity and protected action/tool contracts.
22. Build-Now Requirements: shared communication/untrusted-input/tool-gating seams after reverse-map.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: external support product/channels/customer accounts/pricing.
24. Autonomous Mature State: most routine support resolves automatically with cited knowledge and verified tools; humans handle novel, emotional, high-risk and protected cases.

## Saturation result

Further support branches are onboarding/front-desk/QA/knowledge products already represented.

# Company 046 — Customer Onboarding Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:046`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:046`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-046-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer messages, account changes, migration execution or external deployment.

## Business identity

Purpose: move new customers from signed-up/sold to successfully configured, migrated, trained and activated with the least human intervention while preserving secure account and data boundaries.

Problem: onboarding combines setup, data import, configuration, integrations, training and customer-specific blockers; delays increase churn and service cost.

Value: personalized readiness plans, automated setup/migration where safe, milestone tracking, risk detection and exception escalation.

## Product tree

Onboarding Plan Generator; Setup Checklist; Account/Workspace Provisioning Prep; Data Import/Migration Assistant; Configuration Wizard; Integration Setup; Personalized Product Tours; Training/Learning Paths; Milestone Tracker; Activation/Adoption Analytics; Customer Risk Monitor; Document/Data Collection; Implementation Project Workspace; Enterprise Multi-Team Onboarding; Customer Portal; Health/Success Handoff; Onboarding Benchmarking; API/OEM; Vertical Packs; Managed Onboarding Ops.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: customer/org identity, purchased plan/entitlements, goals/use cases, required data/integrations, owners/roles, tasks/dependencies, due dates, readiness, import validation, config version, training completion, milestone evidence, blockers, risk/confidence, communication preferences, approvals, handoff status, audit.

Customers: SaaS, enterprise software, fintech-adjacent admin products, ecommerce platforms, developer tools, data/analytics vendors, HR/IT software, services with software implementations, marketplaces.

Verticals: B2B SaaS, data migration-heavy systems, developer platforms, finance/admin, HRIS, ecommerce, field-service software, analytics/BI. Regulated customer data requires private/region-specific migration controls.

## Brain / architecture

Brain understands customer goals/plan/product configuration and proposes onboarding sequence, detects blockers and adapts guidance. Deterministic provisioning/import validation/entitlements own system truth. Brain cannot grant entitlements, modify billing, send external messages or migrate production data beyond authorized workflow.

Architecture: customer/project workspace, task DAG, entitlement/profile refs, integration registry, import staging/validation, training content, telemetry/activation metrics, communication/approval workflow, LLM planning/guidance grounded in product docs.

## Agent tree

Onboarding Planner, Requirements/Data Collection Agent, Setup Agent, Migration Agent, Configuration Agent, Integration Agent, Training Agent, Adoption Agent, Risk/Blocker Agent, Customer Communication Draft Agent, Enterprise Coordinator, Handoff/Success Agent, QA/Data Validation Agent.

## Deterministic services

Customer/org registry; entitlement lookup; task/dependency scheduler; import staging; schema validation; integration setup state; provisioning APIs; training completion; milestone/evidence; notification queue; analytics; audit; protected account/data-change gates.

## Workflow

Customer authorized → capture goals/plan → generate dependency plan → collect required data/access → stage/validate import → configure/test integrations → train → verify milestones/activation → resolve blockers/escalate → customer acceptance → handoff to success/support → retain onboarding evidence.

## Integrations / API / data

CRM, billing/entitlements, product/admin APIs, data import/storage, IdP/SSO, support, training/LMS, calendar/comms, analytics, ticketing/project systems. APIs for onboarding/status/tasks/readiness/migrations/milestones/risk/handoff.

Data moat: onboarding templates by product/vertical, migration mappings, blocker/resolution corpus, activation milestone/outcome patterns. Customer data remains isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Customers onboarded, seats, migrations/GB/records, enterprise implementation projects, premium packs, managed onboarding, API/OEM. Distribution through SaaS platforms, implementation partners, CRM/CS ecosystems.

## Security/privacy

Production customer data migration requires staging, provenance, rollback, least privilege and explicit authorization. Entitlements/account roles protected; no secret exposure; customer communications policy/consent; delete temporary migration data.

## Failure / edge cases

Bad source data, schema mismatch, incomplete permissions, integration provider outage, SSO domain error, customer changes goals, partial import, duplicate records, timezone/role confusion, training skipped, billing entitlement mismatch. Use checkpoints, rollback/reconciliation and truthful blocker state.

## Scale/overlap

SMB self-service → enterprise implementation platform. Overlap #60 software migration, #20 cleanup, #45 support, #70 entitlements. #046 focuses customer activation lifecycle.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** customer/org/project identities, entitlement refs, migration staging/rollback, task DAG, evidence/handoff, comms/account protected actions.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center Foundry/workspace/import/Needs Me patterns may generalize after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** customer tenant/auth/billing/entitlement and migration interfaces.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** customer onboarding product/templates/integrations/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** enterprise multi-team implementation automation.

15. Moat Tree: templates/migration maps/blocker corpus/activation outcome data.

17. Risk Tree: customer data corruption, entitlement errors, secrets, poor migration, overcommunication.
18. Scale Tree: self-service→enterprise implementations→multi-product onboarding platform.
19. Spinoff Tree: adjacent #60/#20/#45/#70 already cover migration/cleanup/support/entitlements.

22. Build-Now Requirements: shared Foundry/import/Needs Me patterns after reverse-map.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: external onboarding product/customer portals/pricing.
24. Autonomous Mature State: onboarding plans, checks, migration validation, guidance and risk monitoring run continuously; humans handle customer-specific/protected blockers.

# Company 047 — Privacy Request / DSAR Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:047`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:047`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-047-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no identity acceptance, deletion, disclosure or legal response.

## Business identity

Purpose: orchestrate privacy requests such as access, deletion, correction, portability and opt-out across company systems with identity verification, evidence and deadlines.

Problem: privacy requests require discovering data across many systems, applying jurisdiction/purpose exceptions, coordinating deletion/export and proving completion.

Value: structured intake, system mapping, deadline tracking, scoped execution plans, reconciliation and audit-ready evidence.

## Product tree

Privacy Request Portal; Identity Verification Workflow; Request Type/Jurisdiction Classifier; Data Source Inventory; Data Discovery Orchestrator; Access Export Builder; Deletion Workflow; Correction Workflow; Portability Export; Opt-Out Workflow; Exception/Legal Hold Engine; Deadline/Calendar; Subprocessor/Vendor Request Routing; Data Map/ROPA Crossover; Request Status Portal; Evidence/Audit Package; Appeals/Clarification; API/OEM; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Jurisdiction Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: requester identity, jurisdiction, request type, scope, verified contact/channel, source systems, data categories, purpose, legal hold/exception, due dates, extensions, vendor/subprocessor status, discovery evidence, export/deletion/correction results, residual data, backup handling, owner/legal review, audit and communications.

Customers: SaaS, ecommerce, enterprises, consumer apps, data/AI vendors, marketplaces, HR/admin platforms, privacy/legal/security teams, MSP/consultants.

Verticals: consumer platforms, SaaS, ecommerce, HR, education, health administrative data, finance-adjacent products, advertising/analytics systems. Jurisdiction/legal interpretation requires specialist packs.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain classifies request text, maps likely data sources and flags jurisdiction/exception questions. Deterministic identity verification, policy, deletion/export orchestration and evidence own execution. Brain cannot waive legal obligations, disclose data or delete records itself without protected authority.

Architecture: request state machine, identity verification adapter, data-source catalog/lineage, connector registry, policy/jurisdiction packs, discovery/search, export packaging, deletion/reconciliation engine, vendor workflow, audit ledger, LLM for request classification/explanation grounded in policy.

## Agent tree

Request Intake Agent, Identity Verification Coordinator, Jurisdiction/Policy Agent, Data Discovery Agent, Source Connector Agent, Export Agent, Deletion Coordinator, Correction Agent, Vendor/Subprocessor Agent, Exception/Hold Agent, Deadline Agent, Evidence/Reconciliation Agent, Communication Draft Agent, QA/Privacy Agent.

## Deterministic services

Request registry; identity proof state; deadline scheduler; data-source graph; connectors; subject/entity matching; export builder; deletion/tombstone jobs; backup exception tracking; vendor tasks; audit; retention; protected disclosure/delete/send gates.

## Workflow

Request → identity verification → classify jurisdiction/type/scope → deadline → locate subject across systems → determine exceptions/holds → prepare access/delete/correct plan → legal/privacy review where needed → protected execution → reconcile every source/vendor → package evidence/export → authorized response → close/retain evidence.

## Integrations / API / data

CRM/customer DB, auth, support, marketing, analytics, warehouses, object/vector stores, HRIS, billing, vendors/subprocessors, data catalogs, ticketing, communications. APIs for requests/sources/discovery/actions/status/evidence.

Data moat: source connector/map library, subject resolution, jurisdiction workflow packs and reconciliation patterns; requester/customer data remains isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Requests/year, systems/connectors, seats, enterprise/private, jurisdiction packs, API/OEM, managed privacy operations. Distribution via privacy/legal/security ecosystems, data catalog/GRC integrations and consultants.

## Security/privacy/legal

Highest privacy sensitivity. Strong identity verification, purpose limitation, least privilege, export encryption, no wrong-person disclosure, deletion holds/exceptions, data minimization, auditable access. Product does not replace legal counsel.

## Failure / edge cases

Identity spoof, duplicate requester identities, account merge, legal hold, backup retention, deleted-but-cached data, derived models/embeddings, vendor nonresponse, employee/customer overlap, minors/authorized representatives, deadline extensions. Explicit unknown/exception states and human review.

## Scale/overlap

Small SaaS → enterprise privacy operations → privacy orchestration infrastructure. Overlap #76 PII discovery, #78 retention/deletion, #93 consent, #94 lineage. #047 owns request lifecycle.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** subject identity, data lineage/source registry, retention/deletion/export evidence, protected disclosure/delete, jurisdiction policy packs.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center data governance/retention/privacy interfaces likely affected after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** customer subject mapping, deletion/export orchestration, vendor/subprocessor workflow.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** privacy portal/connectors/jurisdiction product/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global jurisdiction/vendor network.

# Company 048 — Accounts-Payable Verification Brain

**Company ID:** `company:future:048`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:048`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-048-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no payment, vendor, bank-account, accounting or approval action.

## Business identity

Purpose: verify accounts-payable obligations before money leaves a business by reconciling invoices, vendors, purchase orders, receiving evidence, contracts, tax treatment, approval authority and anomaly/fraud signals.

Problem: AP teams face duplicate invoices, vendor impersonation, bank-detail changes, pricing errors, missing PO/receipts, tax mismatches, unauthorized spend and fragmented approval evidence.

Value: higher payment accuracy, faster exception handling, lower fraud/error risk, stronger audit evidence and better cash visibility without turning probabilistic AI into payment authority.

## Complete product tree

Invoice Verification Workspace; Vendor Master Validation; PO/Invoice/Receipt Matching; Contract/Rate Verification; Duplicate Invoice Detection; Bank-Change Risk Gate; Tax/VAT/Sales-Tax Check Adapter; Approval Matrix; Exception Queue; Fraud/Anomaly Scoring; Cash-Timing Recommendations; Payment-Run Preflight; Supplier Portal; AP Inbox Ingestion; Document Extraction; Accounting/ERP Connectors; Audit/Evidence Pack; API/SDK; Batch Verification API; Managed AP Verification; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Industry Packs; Benchmark/Analytics Product.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: invoice OCR/structured intake, supplier identity, remit-to/bank-change history, invoice/PO/receipt/contract line matching, tolerances, quantity/unit/price/tax/currency validation, duplicate/fuzzy duplicate detection, credit memo handling, approval routing, segregation of duties, exception explanations, payment-date recommendations, confidence/evidence, immutable decision history, export/reconciliation and human-review queues.

Customers: SMB finance teams, controllers, AP departments, multi-entity groups, accounting firms, outsourced bookkeeping/AP providers, procurement teams, marketplaces, franchise groups, enterprises.

Verticals: retail/ecommerce, construction, manufacturing, logistics, hospitality, professional services, healthcare administration, property management, nonprofits, education, multi-location businesses. Each may need specialized PO/receiving/tax/workflow packs.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain should understand invoice semantics, supplier history, contract language, normal purchasing patterns, discrepancy context and likely root cause. It may ANALYZE and RECOMMEND approval/hold/investigate/payment timing. It may never autonomously authorize payment, bank-detail change or override financial controls.

Architecture: deterministic matching/rules engine, supplier/entity graph, document extraction pipeline, AP ledger, contract/PO/receipt adapters, anomaly models, policy engine, confidence scoring, explainable evidence graph, LLM for grounded exception interpretation, protected financial-action gate.

## Agent tree

Invoice Intake Agent; Supplier Verification Agent; PO/Receipt Match Agent; Contract Rate Agent; Duplicate/Fraud Agent; Tax Classification Assistant; Approval Coordinator; Exception Investigator; Cash-Timing Analyst; Supplier Communication Draft Agent; Evidence/Audit Agent; Reconciliation Agent; QA/Finance-Control Agent.

## Deterministic services

Invoice parser; line-item matcher; tolerance engine; duplicate fingerprinting; vendor master service; bank-change hold service; approval matrix; tax adapter; accounting sync; idempotency keys; payment-run preflight; immutable evidence ledger; protected payment/bank-change gates.

## Workflow tree

Invoice received → malware/document validation → extract → resolve supplier → compare vendor master/bank state → match PO/receipt/contract → tax/currency/totals checks → duplicate/anomaly/fraud checks → route exception or approval recommendation → required human/authorized approval → payment-run preflight → downstream accounting/payment system action only through protected authority → reconcile settlement → preserve audit evidence.

## Integrations / API / data

ERP/accounting, procurement, banking/payment providers, tax engines, vendor portals, email/document intake, contract repositories, inventory/receiving, identity/SSO, audit/GRC. APIs for invoice ingest, verification, exceptions, supplier risk, approval state, preflight and evidence.

Data: invoices, line items, suppliers, PO/receipts, contracts, bank-change events, approvals, exceptions, payment outcomes, credits/refunds, fraud signals. Sensitive financial/vendor data stays company isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Per invoice/document, AP volume tiers, supplier count, entities, seats, managed service, API usage, enterprise/private deployment, premium fraud/contract/tax packs, verified savings/recovery share where legally and contractually appropriate.

Distribution: accounting/ERP marketplaces, finance consultants, AP automation partners, accounting firms and direct enterprise finance channels.

## Security/privacy/compliance

High financial risk. Least privilege, dual control, bank-change cooling/verification, no AI payment authority, encrypted documents, immutable approvals, supplier impersonation controls, sanctions/compliance adapters where applicable, regional financial-record retention. Product does not replace accountants, tax professionals or legal counsel.

## Failure / edge cases

Partial receipts, split POs, blanket POs, recurring invoices, credit memos, currency conversion, early-pay discounts, duplicate supplier entities, bank mergers, legitimate bank change, invoice number reuse, tax-inclusive pricing, disputed goods, prepayments, intercompany invoices, no-PO spend, manual journals, malicious PDFs. Unknowns must become explicit exceptions rather than guessed matches.

## Scale / overlap

Micro business AP verification → multi-entity enterprise controls → verification API/control plane. Overlap #30 invoice/payment recovery, #32 procurement, #63 vendor onboarding, #73 secret/credential changes, #85 revenue leakage, #86 payment reconciliation. #048 owns pre-payment obligation verification.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** protected financial-action model, supplier/entity identity, evidence/provenance, immutable approvals, idempotency, bank-detail change isolation.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center financial/protected-action and cross-company isolation interfaces may need reverse-map reinforcement.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** customer tenancy, ERP/payment connector abstraction, supplier graph, deterministic match/tolerance engine.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** AP UI, accounting connectors, fraud models, vertical packs, pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global supplier intelligence, cross-customer benchmark signals with privacy-safe aggregation.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: workspace/vendor/3-way match/contracts/duplicates/bank gate/tax/approval/exceptions/fraud/cash/preflight/portal/inbox/API/managed/enterprise/analytics.
2. Feature Tree: extract/vendor/bank/PO/receipt/contract/tax/currency/totals/duplicates/approvals/evidence/exceptions/reconcile.
3. Customer Tree: SMB/controllers/AP/accounting firms/procurement/marketplaces/franchise/enterprise.
4. Vertical Tree: retail/construction/manufacturing/logistics/hospitality/services/health admin/property/nonprofit/education.
5. Brain Tree: invoice/supplier/context analysis and recommendations; payment/bank authority prohibited without separate protected authorization.
6. Agent Tree: intake/vendor/match/contract/duplicate-tax/approval/investigation/cash/comms/evidence/reconciliation/QA.
7. Service Tree: parser/matcher/tolerance/fingerprint/vendor master/bank hold/approval/tax/accounting/idempotency/preflight/audit.
8. Workflow Tree: ingest→verify supplier→match→validate→risk→exception/approval→protected action→settlement reconciliation.
9. Integration Tree: ERP/accounting/procurement/banking/tax/contracts/receiving/email/identity/audit.
10. Data Tree: invoices/lines/suppliers/PO/receipts/contracts/bank events/approvals/exceptions/payments/outcomes.
11. API Tree: ingest/verify/exceptions/supplier/preflight/evidence.
12. Monetization Tree: document/volume/suppliers/entities/seats/API/managed/enterprise/packs/savings share.
13. Distribution Tree: ERP marketplaces/accounting firms/finance consultants/AP partners/direct enterprise.
14. Automation Tree: extraction/matching/risk/routing/reconciliation automated; payment/bank changes gated.
15. Moat Tree: supplier history, discrepancy patterns, connector breadth, verified exception outcomes.
16. Platform Tree: verifier→AP control plane→financial obligation assurance infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: fraud/wrong payment/bank spoof/tax error/duplicate/false match/data leakage.
18. Scale Tree: micro AP→multi-entity→enterprise/global verification API.
19. Spinoff Tree: supplier identity/risk and payment preflight could become modules; adjacent companies already cover procurement/vendor onboarding/reconciliation.
20. Command Center Dependencies: financial governance, identity, protected actions, evidence, connector registry, company isolation, secrets.
21. Design-Now Requirements: money-action taxonomy, supplier/account identity, dual-control/evidence and idempotency contracts.
22. Build-Now Requirements: preserve reusable financial/protected-action and tenant boundaries after portfolio reverse-map.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: AP UI/connectors/fraud models/customer billing/vertical packs.
24. Autonomous Mature State: routine invoices are verified/routed/reconciled automatically; people handle ambiguous suppliers/exceptions and authorize protected financial actions.

## Saturation result

Further coherent branches either become procurement/vendor onboarding/payment reconciliation/revenue-leakage products already represented elsewhere or specialized AP modules under this company.
